blocks.name: Acids & Alkalis
blocks.definition: know that acids in aqueous solution are a source of hydrogen ions and alkalis in a aqueous solution are a source of hydroxide ions

blocks.md:
- When **acids** are added to water, they form positively charged **hydrogen ions** (H<sup>+</sup>)

  - The presence of H<sup>+</sup> ions is what makes a solution acidic
- When **alkalis** are added to water, they form negative hydroxide ions (OH<sup>–</sup>)

  - The presence of the OH<sup>–</sup> ions is what makes the aqueous solution an alkali
- The pH scale is a numerical scale which is used to show how **acidic** or **alkaline** a solution is

  - It is a measure of the amount of the hydrogen ions present in solution

blocks.name: Neutralisation
blocks.definition: know that alkalis can neutralise acids

blocks.md:
- A neutralisation reaction occurs when an acid reacts with an alkali
- When these substances react together in a neutralisation reaction, the **H**<sup>**+**</sup> ions react with the **OH**<sup>**–**</sup> ions to produce water
- Not all reactions of acids are neutralisations

  - For example when a metal reacts with an acid, although a salt is produced there is no water formed so it does not fit the definition of neutralisation

- Neutralisation is very important in the treatment of soils to raise the pH as some crops cannot tolerate pH levels below 7

  - This is achieved by adding bases to the soil such as limestone and quicklime
